pr_title: Fix a job quota related deadlock
pr_body:

#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
In case ResourceQuota is used and sets a max # of jobs, a CronJob may get trapped in a deadlock:
  1. Job quota for a namespace is reached.
  2. CronJob controller can't create a new job, because quota is reached.
  3. Cleanup of jobs owned by a cronjob doesn't happen, because a control loop iteration is finished because of an error to create a job.

To fix this we stop early quitting from a control loop iteration when cronjob reconciliation failed and always let old jobs to be cleaned up.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

issue_context.title: CronJob gets stuck when jobs quota is reached
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

We (in Booking.com) run CronJobs in Kubernetes clusters with ResourceQuota's defined. When quota for # of jobs is reached we observed that CronJobs:
1. stop scheduling new jobs (because quota is reached),
2. don't clean the old jobs (despite # of jobs > history allows and the fact that it would unblock the CronJob new Jobs). 

The only way to progress is to remove enough Jobs to make room for a new Job in namespace quota. When we do that manually, the CronJob kicks in.

The workaround we found around the internet is to specify `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` for the job template. But it's not ideal as it's not a history-based limit, but a time-based limit, and often you want to have the last N jobs to be around for debugging.

### What did you expect to happen?

When jobs quota is reached and # of cronjob jobs exceeds specified the history limit, these jobs are deleted giving room for new jobs to run.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```yaml
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: job-quota
  namespace: default
spec:
  hard:
    count/jobs.batch: "1"
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: hello-world-cronjob
spec:
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 0
  schedule: "* * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
            - name: hello-world
              image: bash
              command: ["bash", "-c", "sleep 80"]
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

1. Wait for a first Job to be created (which will fill up the jobs quota) at X minute.
2. A job for X + 1 will fail to be created (because quota won't allow, and X job is still running).
3. All future attempts to create a new job by the controller will fail (check `kubectl get events --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail`, you'll see re-occuring `Error creating job: jobs.batch "hello-world-cronjob-28187648" is forbidden: exceeded quota: job-quota, requested: count/jobs.batch=1, used: count/jobs.batch=1, limited: count/jobs.batch=1`).
4. The first job will never be cleaned (although it will be eligible, since history is 0).

### Anything else we need to know?

Looks like the problem was introduced in the `cronjob_controllerv2.go` implementation: if `jm.syncCronJob` returned an error, we return from the function and never invoke `jm.cleanupFinishedJobs`.:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L199-L213

In the old `cronjob_controller.go` implementation this was not the case:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0f77da5bd4809927e15d1658fb4aa8f13ad890a5/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controller.go#L137-L138

review_comments: without much experience on this controller this change looks like an important behavior change in the controller

There is exactly the same if-statement below, which is going to be executed unless there is a panic in the code, as there are no return-statements in-between anymore: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/16173c23baa3a6a7ad19233c963d165dc7f602d9/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L208-L214

Could we nevertheless make attempt to update the status here, but with different error handling, and a comment in both places about the situation?

Logging that the status update failed is helpful; it's just the `return` statements that create a problem.

Any other logic refactor that ensures we attempt `cleanupFinishedJobs()` is also fine by me. Ideally we don't drop any observability along with that change.

Updated the PR description (per @sftim suggestion) to better explain why the if-statement was removed, please tell me if it clarifies things.

As for the comments:
> Could we nevertheless make attempt to update the status here, but with different error handling, and a comment in both places about the situation?

If I make an attempt to update the status here, it will result in making 2 status updates instead of just 1 that is enough + a copy-paste in the code that is not needed anymore (it was only needed because we had a return-statement). I'm not sure what is the concern here, why do we need to do this?

> Logging that the status update failed is helpful; it's just the return statements that create a problem.

We're still logging the status update failure in the code that follows: https://github.com/ASverdlov/kubernetes/blob/16173c23baa3a6a7ad19233c963d165dc7f602d9/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L208-L214

Maybe we should set `updateStatus` to true, but defer the update?

I'd like to see a clear comment that shows why this change is right. It might be, but I want the code and PR to explain why.

I found another problem in the code: because I got rid of a return-statement here, we no longer report the error back to the `processNextWorkItem` function, which has logic to re-queue the item in case of error.

I could save the error into a distinguishable error (like `reconciliationErr` and report it in the very end instead of `return nil, nil`), but it seems more dangerous, so I restored the copy-paste.

Now the logic is hopefully easier to verify, but you can clearly see 2 blocks of copy-pasted code here:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d2267b2591e78aebad0346bf9716e7119cae9741/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L203C1-L213
and here:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d2267b2591e78aebad0346bf9716e7119cae9741/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L217-L227

Looks good! I updated the code following your suggestion.

This required changing the signature of `jm.syncCronJob` since it wouldn't make sense for it to still be generating the cronjobCopy, updateStatus if it's not the first modification. I extracted cronjobCopy and updateStatus creation outside and passing them as pointers to both `jm.syncCronJob` and `jm.cleanupFinishedJobs` to make this combination of variables more explicit in the code and make functions order-independent.

Please take another look.
